title.narrative: Core support to Innovation Centre Kosovo

description.narrative:
Innovation Centre Kosovo has requested a core funding of 14 million SEK to carry out the Strategy Plan "'Scaling up and further consolidation of startup ecosystem 2019-2022'' during the period 2019-2022. The total amount of the budget is 5,3 million Euro.
The cooperation with Innovation Centre Kosovo (ICK) during the first phase of core support 2015-2018 has worked well, both in terms of quality and timely deliveries. Almost all the results have exceeded the foreseen plans. For six years, ICK's incubator department has launched 18 calls for proposals and 2 cross sectorial calls (Women edition and FinTech). Over 200 start ups were accepted to be part of the ICK’s incubator, where 65 were women co-founders and out of which 170 new registered companies have been established. Total number of internal training courses delivered was 210 to almost 3000 trainees. Internal event organized were 356 (over 450 including events co-organized in partnership with others) attended by more than 40 000 participants. Sida has been satisfied with a cooperation and achieved results.
The overall new objective is to support the aspiration of individuals, private companies, government and foreign investors for development, by propelling innovative ideas and introducing new products, services and operations that improve the lives of Kosovo citizens, and increase competitiveness of local economy through utilizing services and network of Innovation Centre Kosovo.
ICK Strategic plan 2019-2022 is structured around the following key pillars:
1. Innovation-startup enabling environment is one of the most important pillars that ICK will focus on. Start-up incubator will offer services such as training, coaching, mentoring, and other forms of capacity building and transfer of know-how will be continued under the upcoming programing cycle. On the other hand, ICK will offer technological space for all interested star-ups and businesses, and will continue to support start-ups and businesses through grants and innovation funds.
2. Empowering entrepreneurship and promoters of Innovation: ICK’s vision for the future entails additional efforts in inclusion of marginalized groups, spinoffs, minority communities, diaspora, civil society, and the government. This will be implemented by identifying the needs, organizing entrepreneurial events throughout Kosovo, increasing skills, networking and improving skills to improve employment and self-employment.
3. Focusing on key priority sectors: ICK will diversify sectoral presence and included, social entrepreneurship, sustainable innovation, and government innovation. Promoting innovation and increased application of technology across different sectors, is crucial also for increasing effects across the society and contribute to its overall modernization.
The overall budget for implementation of the ICK's Strategic Plan 2019-2022 is planned to be 5,3 million Euro, out of which: Sida (2019-2022) will give a core support budget with an amount of 14 MSEK (1,4 million Euro), GIZ (2018-2020) with 904 230 Euro, Norway (2018-2020) with 234 438 Euro, EU/EDF/ICK (2018-2020) with 316 668 Euro, European Fund for Southeast Europe (EFSE) (2018-2019) with 92 833 Euro, Kosovo Ministry of Innovation and Entrepreneurship (2018-2019) with 196 244 Euro and ICK’s own funding is planned to be 760 000 Euro. There is a budget gap of 1,4 million Euro for 2020-2021, which is expected to be filled in with contributions from other possible donors.

Vision: Modern society in which innovation and entrepreneurship are an integrated part of our culture & society, and a major factor of development and improvement of the living standard of all citizens.Mission:ICK aims to advance innovation and entrepreneurship to new levels, in which entrepreneurial spirit and culture of innovation are reflected amongst individuals, companies and government, through creating a functional ecosystem in which ventures are supported to growth and sustainability.Overall Objective:ICK will support the aspiration of individuals, private institutions, governments and foreign investors to achieve development by generating innovative ideas and introducing new products, services and operations that improve the overall quality of life of Kosovo citizens, and increase competitiveness of local economy, through creating of a functional ecosystem Specific Objective 1. Contribute to improving Innovation and startup enabling environment This objective will be reached by providing direct financial support for startups and innovative SMEs through Grant Funds, through government and CSO support and through providing new services for start-ups and SMEs such as:- Improved market access information and linkages for startups, SMEs and foreign direct investors;- Promotional services through digitalization;- Physical and technological infrastructure such as free rent space in Pristina and expanding in 3 other cities;- Access to finance through matching funds, Innovation fund, Angel Club, Crowdfunding platforms and partner with accelerator; Specific Objective 2: Improving the skills of youth and improve employment and self-employment prospects Increasing and improving the skills of youth and competences relevant to todays market and improving employment and self-employment will be reached through:- Improved professional trainings - Training large number of youth in the areas identified as being in high demand. This would create critical mass of seasoned professionals to satisfy the needs and export aspirations of Kosovo companies;- Fostering entrepreneurship through incubation, mentoring and voucher schemes;- Technical services for its beneficiaries including but not limited to office space, hosting and other services;- Facilitate Internships, Job Placements and Direct Employment of students at existing companies. Specific Objective 3: Support and Promote entrepreneurship and Innovation ICK aims to advance innovation and entrepreneurship to new levels and integrate them in our culture. This objective will be reached to:- Constantly promote and increase awareness on the importance of innovation and entrepreneurship through, so that ventures are supported to growth and sustainability;- Have a high participation of target audiences in our innovations programs and schemes;- Organize entrepreneurial events throughout Kosovo; networking gatherings, connect participants to potential collaborators, mentors and even investorsintroducing them to new possibilities and exciting opportunities;- Increase the number of women/girls in ICT sector. Specific Objective 4: Increase of innovation and modernization of key sectors of interestAs part of the new strategy pillars and activities, ICK has identified Technology, Sustainable Innovation, Social Entrepreneurship and Government Innovation as four main innovation priority sectors. By increasing activities that lead to innovating and modernizing these sectors, ICK will create an impact in the ecosystem. This objective will be achieved by:- Introducing and encouraging the application of technology in relevant sectors;- Support cross-sectorial projects through incubator department;- Seek ways to engage relevant stakeholders in innovation and technology application.

description.narrative:
In 2023, the Innovation Centre Kosovo (ICK) advanced its mission to promote entrepreneurial growth and innovation through its Startup Support Program and Training Events & PR Department. Bio365 Kosova Turning Waste into Sustainable Energy Sammanfattande resultatuppdatering Conclusion on Performance Contribution ID: 12391 3 (9) Bio365 Kosova, a womenled startup, addressed a significant environmental challenge by transforming biomass waste from essential oil production into a sustainable business model. With support from ICKs Startup Support Program, including an €8,000 grant and 20% cofinancing, the company invested in pellet production and biomass grinding equipment. This enabled the production of bio pellets, an eco-friendly energy source now used to power their distillation and drying processes. Even the ash generated from the pellets is repurposed as organic fertilizer, establishing a circular economy that reduces waste and lowers costs. By integrating sustainability into their operations, Bio365 Kosova has significantly reduced energy and raw material expenses. Their innovative approach not only enhances profitability but also attracts investment, promoting long-term business growth while safeguarding the environment. Kosovo Glass Recycling-Turning Waste into Opportunity Kosovo Glass Recycling is committed to contributing to a more sustainable future for Kosovo. With support from ICKs Startup Support Program, including an €8,000 grant and 20% cofinancing, the company expanded its operations by acquiring new production machinery that increased its glass recycling capacity. This upgrade allows the company to serve more clients and divert larger quantities of glass waste from landfills. Additionally, the startup launched a user friendly website, improving customer engagement. The grants impact extends beyond environmental gains it also drives economic growth. Kosovo Glass Recycling has already hired one new employee and plans further workforce expansion as operations scale up. By creating jobs and promoting sustainable practices, the startup exemplifies how targeted support can drive both business growth and environmental responsibility. Training departmentaddressing skills gaps in the job market In 2023, ICKs Training Department played a crucial role in developing local talent and addressing key skills gaps in the job market. Through focused training programs, individuals were equipped with highdemand skills, creating a clear pathway from education to employment. Two standout success stories from the year highlight the departments impact. Mr. Fabian Berisha from trainee to full-time employee and educator Fabian Berishas success exemplifies the effectiveness of ICKs training initiatives. After completing the "DevOps and Kubernetes" course, he secured an internship at Apstellar, an ICK alumni startup. Fabians performance earned him a full-time role within the company, and he later returned to ICK as an assistant lecturer in the same course that launched his career. His journey illustrates the Training Departments ability to foster both employment opportunities and a cycle of continuous learning within the community. Ms. Aida Sopi from student to digital marketing specialist Ms. Sopis career trajectory showcases the transformative power of ICKs training programs. After completing courses in social media and digital marketing, she secured a position as a Digital Marketing Specialist at Tive, a global leader in supply chain visibility technology. Aidas success has made her a role model for aspiring professionals, and she has been invited by ICK to inspire young women by sharing her career journey. Her story demonstrates how ICKs training programs empower individuals to build successful careers while contributing to their communities by mentoring others. Overall, during 2023, ICK achieved significant outcomes aligned with its program objectives, including awarding EUR 70,000 in grants to 10 startups through the Green Grant Call and distributing EUR 17,000 in prizes to 17 startups. Mentoring and consultancy services were provided to 43 startups, leading to the creation of 28 new jobs, with strong representation from women entrepreneurs. Over 50 startups participated in local and international events, boosting market presence and networking. ICK also supported technological advancements by providing Amazon Web Services credits worth USD 22,000 to 4 startups. Additionally, 37 professional training courses and workshops were held for 655 participants, nearly half of whom were women. ICK conducted 58 outreach events, engaging around 5,000 individuals, and strengthened partnerships with organizations like UNDP, USAID, and GIZ.
Results 2024: Startup Support Program Electric Mobility LLC Driving Kosovos EV Revolution Forward Electric Mobility LLC, a pioneering startup in sustainable transport, has taken significant strides in building Kosovos electric vehicle (EV) infrastructure. With support from a grant program, the company procured three 22kW EV AC chargers for public use and partnered with GIZ and the Municipality of Prishtina to install two of them at Germia Park Parking. A third charger was installed and commissioned at the Prishtina Parking Center as a public demo unit, increasing visibility and encouraging EV adoption. The chargers are now listed on major platforms like Google Maps, Apple Maps, and OEM navigation systems, boosting public accessibility. Despite delays caused by municipal restructuring, which postponed the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) and installation at Germia Park, Electric Mobility LLC continues to drive forward. Plans for the next phase include using demo units for promotional activities, encouraging EV usage, expanding the charger network citywide and nationally, and developing a broader collaboration framework with the Municipality to strengthen Kosovos green mobility landscape.
More than a Cup Brewing Growth Beyond Borders More than a Cup, a growing startup in the sustainable coffee accessories market, has significantly expanded its operations through strategic investments in production and marketing. With grant support, the team purchased essential machinery, secured long-term packaging supplies, and established in-house sleeve production, while also investing in digital marketing and professional equipment to enhance their working environment. These upgrades boosted production capacity by over 200%, positioning the company for regional growth. As a result, More than a Cup secured a major distribution agreement in North Macedonia, enabling large-scale orders, and is in the final stages of expanding into Montenegro. Additionally, the team resolved a key challenge in e-commerce by partnering with the Post of Kosovo, allowing them to process online orders across 36 countries, paving the way for international sales and brand recognition.
Skills and Development Program Dorela Peja, Graphic Design & Motion Design Training Dorela Peja was the recipient of a full scholarship from CloudAstro to pursue the Graphic Design and Motion Design & Animation courses at ICK. After successfully completing both courses, she was initially given the opportunity to start working at AFS Digital, a digital marketing company. Her success in this role eventually led to a full-time position at Behamics, a company established as part of a project with OTTO, Germanys largest online retailer, aimed at reducing product returns using Behavioral Science.
Erblina Shkodra, DevOps and Kubernetes Fundamentals Training Erblina successfully completed the "DevOps and Kubernetes" training at ICK and, after her outstanding performance, secured a full-time position at CloudAstro. CloudAstro is the go-to destination for businesses looking to scale up their operations using cloud technology and highly trained professionals in this field. CloudAstro's specialists are experts in IT services and IT consulting, focusing primarily on providing advanced cloud solutions for businesses. The company is based in Munich, Bavaria, and enables transformation, growth, and competitive advantage through cloud services.
